'''Marco Fontani'''<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.unifi.it/p-doc2-2013-000000-F-3f2a3d32342d2e-0.html |title=University Of Florence profile |access-date=2016-07-31}}</ref> (born 5 May 1969 in [[Florence]]) is a chemist and [[History of Chemistry|chemistry historian]], author of over 120 publications in materials chemistry, organometallic chemistry, electrochemistry and the history of chemistry. He is also a member of the board of directors<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.consiglio.regione.toscana.it/upload/eda/pubblicazioni/pub4064.pdf |title=Ugo Schiff Conference Proceedings, scientific committee members list |access-date=2017-03-31}}</ref> of the Italian National Society of History of Chemistry (Gruppo Nazionale di Storia e Fondamenti della Chimica).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gnfsc.it/page5/page12/page12.html |title=GNSC members list |access-date=2016-07-31}}</ref>

He wrote the books: ''The Lost Elements: The Periodic Table's Shadow Side''<ref>{{cite book | last1 = Fontani | first1 = Marco | last2 = Costa | first2 = Mariagrazia | last3 = Orna | first3 = Mary Virginia | year = 2014 | title = The Lost Elements: The Periodic Table's Shadow Side | publisher= Oxford University Press|page= 576pp|isbn=9780199383344 }};</ref> and ''Chemistry and Chemists in Florence: From the Last of the Medici Family to the European Magnetic Resonance Center''.<ref>{{cite book | last1 = Fontani | first1 = Marco | last2 = Costa | first2 = Mariagrazia | last3 = Orna | first3 = Mary Virginia | year = 2016 | title = Chemistry and Chemists in Florence: From the Last of the Medici Family to the European Magnetic Resonance Center | publisher= Springer-Verlag|page= 136pp|isbn=978-3319308548 }};</ref> Both edited in Italian and English.

He has been working at the Department of Organic Chemistry at the [[University of Florence]] since 2003.
